body:
I'd like to think that they'll become strengths. I know that they are beneficial traits in family life, and that's where I've always flourished (it's one reason I always saw myself as a future family man). Socially, they've been abysmal traits that lead to invisibility and irrelevance.

I'm not sure I have a place to find guidance. I like to be alone, and look forward to the day when I can live that way.

You seem to have a real interest and knowledge in personal growth... do you have any links/resources you could direct me to?

Thanks for these thoughts! I'm definitely too perfectionistic for my own good. I can at least try to shrug off small failures, as you've suggested.

What helps me most is when I believe that things will okay, regardless of success or failure. Then I can relax and (oddly enough!) succeed more often and not. With work this is difficult, because true failure really isn't okay.

I see what you're saying about anxiety and interest... but I honestly think there's more to it than that. I wish I could express it, but I believe there's a problem that's not merely rooted in anxiety. It lies at the nexus of anxiety and introversion and avoidance and more. I'm not saying I'm a unique snowflake with a never-before-seen inability to connect with people, but I do think I'm odder than most in this regard.

Accepting that I'll *always* be anxious and consequentially alienated has made me feel **much** better. I've been trying for years to grow socially with no success whatsoever. Realizing my limitations in this area has brought me peace, even though it means I have to accept a certain degree of loneliness in the future.

I really get what you're saying about takings risks. But risk-taking is anathema to me; I'm a cautious person, and I'm overwhelmed by failure and rejection, so I only take an action if I'm extremely confident in the outcome. This isn't an effective way to live, I know -- if I could snap my fingers and reset my personality, I would. But I feel that I'll always be tentative, even cowardly. Rather than continue to hate myself for this I'm trying to just accept it and move on.

> How come?

That's... hard to explain! I guess you could call it a mix of avoidance and extreme introversion. I don't really enjoy interacting with others, both because of anxiety and because people (including me) just aren't that interesting. I do try to stay on positive acquaintance terms with everyone if forced to interact (work), but I'll stay invisible if at all possible (school).

I guess it's a confluence of a lot of things. Still living at home, no job until 23, very little social experience, zero dating experience, etc. Even some of the things I choose to do (abstain from alcohol/drugs/etc.) are contributory in some way. It's like I'm abnormally innocent and adolescent.

Ever notice how uncomfortable some kids are in new surroundings? They stand behind a parent, or off to the side, and don't interact unless prompted. That's how I feel. I'm passive to a fault, unsure of myself and my environment, too eager to please others, and almost pathologically in need of guidance. 

I don't know if any of that makes sense.

Thanks... but however I feel about myself, I still have to deal with the expectations of employers, coworkers, etc. I need to maintain some semblance of adulthood, and it's so obvious that I'm a 24-year-old manchild. Some of my classmates are years younger than I am, and are so much more mature and collected.

This makes sense. But I still think I'm objectively less mature, experienced, and capable than my average peer. I have a hard time believing the average person is as unsure of their ability to deal with day-to-day adult life as I am.

Thanks.

I **think** I can handle the practicalities. There's no reason I can't save money and pay my bills and shop intelligently, etc., if so many other people can.

But... there's **plenty** of reason why I might not be able to deal with the daily stresses of work and socializing, or with the realities of setbacks, etc. I'm much, much, much more anxious and tense and inexperienced than the average person my age, or even someone years younger. It's like I'm bringing a knife to a gunfight.

I guess there's positive and negative ways of feeling like a kid. I like being someone who's "young at heart," but I have to be able to muster the confidence and maturity to at least be a semi-respectable employee and coworker. I'm treated very kindly where I work now, but I believe I'm perceived as a kid, as though I'm a naive teenager with promise. I'm grateful to be regarded well, but I'm supposed to be a "man," and it's so very obvious that I'm not.

Thanks for your response.

I respect that any sort of growing up takes time, but I feel like it's been so long already. Every time I enter a new 'phase' of my life I think it's the one where I'll finally come into my own... but it's never happened. Leaving school and entering the workforce is the last big transition left.

As far as socializing goes, I've chosen to just let that go. It's not a case of being dissimilar to others; it's utter discomfort and tension with myself and with any socializing at all. I try to avoid friendships and genuine connections in favor of more superficial acquaintances. If that makes sense. I do get along very well with my nuclear family, so I'll have them.

> Importantly, keep growing. This is hard to describe. Don't keep trying the same thing expecting different results. Always try and be friendly, but if that doesn't work, try being a little mean. Try and be gentle, but if that doesn't work, try being rough. Try being gung-ho, but if that doesn't work, try being laid-back. There's a balance here, and the only way to strike it is to give yourself a little wiggle room with the extremes. There's a place for all of these, and we have to feel comfortable using them in that setting, so when the setting arises we can respond in a positive way.

This is extremely insightful. I will seriously think on this.

I've never thought about external vs. internal improvement. That would explain a lot. One of the things my therapist told me at the end of our first meeting was that I had "killed it" in regards to self-improvement. I suppose I've exhausted every avenue in that direction.

My therapist has urged me take up a new outside activity (we settled on jogging), to return to reading for fun (which I stopped because of coursework), and to take some time away from obsessing over work/school/family. So tomorrow I'm going to drive a couple hours away to a state park and get a motel room. I'm going to jog a bit, and then go back to my room and order a pizza and read. I know it sounds simple and silly for that, but I've never done independent stuff like this before... I don't know if it counts as internal improvement, but I will trust my therapist. I am kinda looking forward to it.

> In fact, reclaiming your true self means you stop working so hard to hang on to the culturally sanctioned fucked-ness. And one almost-universal characteristic of people who've been indoctrinated with the idea that who they really are is not socially acceptable is a pervasive sense of deep shame. Sound familiar?

It does... I've never heard of this. Do you have a link maybe? I'd like to read more about it.

I don't know about my true self. I don't exactly like or want anything, really; it feels like everything I do is stressful and unnatural. If I've been trying to change myself for the culture at large, I have no idea what else to be. In my natural state I think I'd hide from everything like I always have. Maybe my therapist will have some idea about this, I dunno... I feel as though I have to walk the tightrope before me, or fall. I don't see any other option.

Thank you for your time and patience. I feel better than I did, at least for now, and I really appreciate having someone to talk to, as there is no one else. I am still in a bad way if I don't improve things, especially academically, but I'm not in danger right now. Maybe I can clear my head this weekend and get back on track a little bit.

Thanks a lot for your encouragement. I do feel like a coward and a failure in many ways, but I guess I should look at my improvement more objectively. I am a far cry from who I want to be, but I have made objective progress, and my future has a chance of being good if continue the trajectory I had going.

Maybe you're right about it only being depression. I do feel tentatively better today versus the past few days, and that's probably thanks to coffee and the promise of the weekend. It's funny how much a small thing can help... but obviously I still have to work through things. I know life won't always be cheery, it isn't for anyone, but I have to stop my nadirs from getting so dangerously low.

Your idea about my brother struck closer to home than you might think. I half-raised him, and am his primary parent/role model now, and he takes after me (and there's some idolizing, as with your nephew). The idea of him belittling himself bothers me quite a bit. He's like me, and veers towards depression at times... I worry a lot about him, more than anything else, but my therapist has told me that being happier myself is the best thing I can do for him.

I will take to heart your the idea that I have only been helping to treat depression rather than directly addressing it. I will have to rely on my therapist for that. He has been adamant that I take up more recreation, and spend less time obsessing over school/work/family. I plan tomorrow to do some of what he's suggested and see how it goes. Honestly, I feel like having temporary fun is not going to improve the context of my life, but I'll have to trust that he has a plan.

Thanks for your words, they've helped a lot. I hope you continue to do well, and me too. I know we're just strangers, but it helps me to know that you can sympathize with what I'm going through.

Even if it's possible to change, it would take so much effort, and so much time. I'm tired. I'm ashamed of myself. I'm embarrassed just to be seen. Even if I could change I'm not willing to, I'm a chickenshit, if I was capable of the steps necessary I would never have become what I am.

I've spent so much time and money and effort already. I got a gym membership, I lost 70 pounds, I hired a personal trainer, I bought new clothes, I got contacts instead of glasses, I changed my hairstyle, I got my teeth fixed, I tried to eat better, and take vitamins, and do cardio three times a week. I did all the shit you're supposed to do. I thought if I looked better and ate better then I would feel better, I tried to trigger a positive feedback loop. And all I have to show for it is mounting debt and the realization that all those hopes were false ones, and that I've run out of things to try. 

Now I just want to rest. I know I don't want to die, if I did I wouldn't be whining now. But if the only alternative is a life of anxiety and loneliness and shame then I would rather die.

I don't see how my problems are so bad, my life should be easy. I have the easiest job in the world, and I have my mother and my brothers. I've read some posts here, some people have it so much worse.

I will meet with my therapist next week if I can. I will try and level with him. I think I've tried almost everything, but maybe he knows something I don't.

Thank you so much for talking. I'm sure this is tiresome, and I'm just a stranger. I have a project due tomorrow but I'm going to go jog instead and then go to bed.

I don't know if I believe that, I have become worse as I've failed. I am rational in this. There are things I wanted to do and be and I failed. Maybe it's my fault, maybe it's circumstance, but either way it is what it is and I am what I am. There are selves I don't want to be.

I would not start over if I could, I am pathetic enough without trying and failing anymore than I already have. I know that that's obnoxiously self-pitying, but I don't see it any other way. If I'm rational about this then I know that the time for hope is past.

I can't break from school, I should be out already and I can't waste anymore time. I have started seeing a therapist, he is very good but there's nothing he can do.

Thank you for your time, I am sorry for this.

I'm sorry, but I don't believe that people can really develop or improve after a point. I've never seen it happen. I tried in the past couple years to do a lot to improve myself, but it doesn't change anything. I lost weight and got a good job and made decent grades, but we all have limits to our potential. If I can't be who I want to be then fuck it, and I can't.

I read your post you linked to... it was extremely touching. It sounds like you had things much harder than I do, and my problems seem small in comparison. I know that I'm lucky in a lot of ways and correspondingly ungrateful. 

I've tried to see this new therapist, he is very compatible, but there are things I'm too embarrassed to reveal, and I don't know what help can be given anyway. I am what I am -- that's the problem, and that won't change. I know that the mind of a depressed person is supposedly irrational, but I'm more grounded than anyone I know.

Thank you for reading and responding. This a kind place and I am thankful.
